cards.explanation: The answer is that Absalom will overtake them and strike the city. David says Absalom, his son, “…will soon overtake us, heap disaster on us, and put the city to the sword.” When a king says "We must leave quickly…" he's not talking about beating traffic, friends. The danger he names is Absalom catching up.

The answer is False. “Then the king set out, and his entire household followed him.” That's the whole household on the move, friends. He does leave ten concubines behind to take care of the palace. So nobody in the household stayed home on a lazy day.
The answer is palace. The text says David left behind ten concubines “…to take care of the palace.” Everyone else in the household goes with him, friends. It's a quiet detail in a very loud day.

The answer is that Ittai says wherever the king goes, he will be there. Ittai says, “…wherever my lord the king may be, whether it means life or death, there will your servant be!” Remember, friends, David had just told him he was a foreigner who arrived only yesterday.

The answer is True. After Ittai's promise, David says, “March on then…” and Ittai marches past with all his men and all the little ones who were with him. David gave the man a way out and he didn't take it, friends. Ittai had just said he would be with the king, whether it means life or death. This is him doing exactly that.

The answer is wilderness. As the king crosses the Kidron Valley, “…all the people also passed toward the way of the wilderness.” That's the direction of the whole crowd, friends, not just David. Nobody's packing for a good time out there.

The answer is that the LORD will bring David back to see the ark again. David says, “If I find favor in the eyes of the LORD, He will bring me back and let me see both it and His dwelling place again.” He's handing the whole matter to the LORD instead of holding on to the ark himself. I think that took a lot of trust, friends.

The answer is that David says to let the LORD do whatever seems good to Him. David says, “But if He should say, ‘I do not delight in you,’ then here I am; let Him do to me whatever seems good to Him.” That's a king with nothing in his hands, putting himself in the LORD's. It's a hard sentence to say out loud, friends.

The answer is word from Zadok in the city. David tells Zadok, the priest, “…I will wait at the fords of the wilderness until word comes from you to inform me.” He sends the priests back to Jerusalem and says he'll wait at the fords for their word. That's a lot of trust sent back down the road, friends.

The answer is True. The text says, “…all the people with him covered their heads and went up, weeping as they went.” David's head is covered, and so is everyone else's, friends. This is a whole mountain of people walking up together.

The answer is that David asks the LORD to turn Ahithophel's counsel into foolishness. Ahithophel is now among Absalom's conspirators, and David pleads, “O LORD, please turn the counsel of Ahithophel into foolishness!” Notice where he takes the news, friends: straight to the LORD. He asks about the advice, not about the man himself. That's a prayer prayed on the move, while he's walking and weeping.

The answer is to thwart Ahithophel's counsel. David tells Hushai, “…you can thwart the counsel of Ahithophel for me if you return to the city…” Hushai the Archite, David's friend, is being sent in as David's man on the inside, friends. David has just asked the LORD to turn that counsel into foolishness, so this is a job on the same problem.

The answer is False. David says, “Will not Zadok and Abiathar the priests be there with you? Report to them everything you hear from the king’s palace.” He wants Hushai telling the priests everything, friends. That's a secret that's meant to travel.

The answer is Ahimaaz and Jonathan. David says the priests' two sons, Ahimaaz son of Zadok and Jonathan son of Abiathar, are there with them, and tells Hushai, “Send them to me with everything you hear.” So David's plan is for the news to go from Hushai to the priests, then out with the two sons, friends. That's a three-stop delivery route.
